title: Worked example
displayTitle: Turning a weak topic sentence into a strong one
body:
A first draft often opens a paragraph like this:

"There are many factors that affect climate change, and this essay will talk about some of them."

It fills space but makes no claim, so the reader learns nothing about where the paragraph is heading. Compare a stronger version:

"Although emissions dominate the debate, this paragraph argues that land use is the factor most often underestimated."

The stronger sentence names a specific position the paragraph will defend, signals the line of argument, and gives the reader something they could agree or disagree with. The move to copy: from listing topics to staking a claim.
instruction: Open the worked example and compare the weaker and stronger versions.
